items.title: IREN Fell 4% on Cipher’s Miss, Then Jumped 10%. Here’s What Its November 5 Report Has to Settle
items.summary: Key TakeawaysIREN fell 4% on Nov. 2 after Cipher Digital missed revenue estimates, then jumped 10% the next morning as AI data center stocks rebounded.

items.title: Credo Sinks 10% as Democratic Sweep Hits AI Data Center Stocks: “Biggest Worry”
items.summary: Key TakeawaysCredo fell 10% today as AI data center stocks sold off after Democrats won Congress and the Texas governor’s race. Credo’s growth depends on data centers that voters in Texas want to limit.

items.title: Super Micro Has More Going for It Than Meets the Eye
items.summary: Supermicro shares have sold off hard even as its order backlog hit record levels and a preliminary quarter beat guidance. A single-digit forward multiple on a company growing faster than Dell raises a question worth examining before November 3.

items.title: Nike Climbs 7% as Dow Rally Lifts Consumer Stocks; Deckers Gains 7%, Lululemon Rises 6%
items.summary: A broad market rally is dragging battered footwear giants off their lows, but rising margins and cost cuts tell only half the story at Nike, where the company openly warns its biggest market is about to get worse.

items.title: Super Micro Falls 4% Despite Blowout Quarter as Margin Worries and Data Center Backlash Weigh; Dell Sinks 8%, Hewlett Packard Enterprise Drops 6%
items.summary: Super Micro's blowout earnings sent the stock tumbling instead of soaring, and the reason involves a collision of shrinking margins, one enormous customer, and a wave of ballot measures that could reshape where AI gets built.

items.title: These Were the Best-Performing Asset Classes in October. Will They Continue to Outperform?
items.summary: Real estate and commodities outperformed other asset classes during the month.

items.title: Apple’s Pain Could Be Micron’s Gain as Memory Prices Surge
items.summary: Memory prices are climbing fast, and that single cost is splitting two tech giants onto opposite sides of a trade. One company's suffering feeds the other's record margins, and the gap between them keeps widening.
